messages.content: Using only search results from the enabled Protocol Search tool (do not use its fetch operation, general web search, or direct web fetching), design an end-to-end protocol for long-duration three-dimensional tracking of a fluorescently labeled, mobile subcellular structure in living cells. I need high axial precision and short imaging intervals, but repeated z-stacks cause too much delay and phototoxicity. Include microscope setup or modifications, calibration, the live acquisition and control workflow, validation, downstream analysis, checkpoints, and practical timing. Use only the available pre-July evidence and label unsupported details as assumptions.

I searched the permitted protocol records using search-result metadata only and drafted a feedback-tracking plan. Before finalizing it I need the actual structure and label, imaging depth, required interval and duration, available microscope hardware, and whether custom scanning or controller hardware is acceptable. I would also normally read the returned sources in full, but that would require the prohibited fetch operation.

Use one bright GFP-LacI-marked nuclear locus in budding yeast, one color, within about 2–3 µm of the coverslip. Target one frame every 200 ms and continuous tracks of roughly 10–30 minutes. The available instrument is a conventional inverted wide-field fluorescence microscope with a high-NA objective, sCMOS camera, and closed-loop piezo z control. Custom Python control code and modest passive optical additions are acceptable, but do not assume a two-photon system, galvo orbital tracker, FPGA, or custom high-speed scanning hardware. Continue with search-result metadata only; do not fetch the papers, and label all unsupported values as assumptions.
